You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Duration: two and a half hours.

questions.enonce_markdown:
How does the regular intake of large quantities of alcohol affect:

(i) Individuals

(ii) The society? *(4, 5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Effects on individuals**

1. **Liver damage**: it can lead to **cirrhosis** of the liver.
2. **Damage to the brain and nervous system**: loss of self-control, slow reactions, poor judgement and memory loss.
3. **Addiction** (alcoholism): the person depends on alcohol.
4. Damage to the **stomach** (ulcers), **heart** and blood vessels (high blood pressure).
5. **Malnutrition**, loss of money and of employment; for a pregnant woman, harm to the unborn baby.

(Any four.)

**(ii) Effects on society**

1. More **road accidents** caused by drunk drivers.
2. More **crime, violence and fights**, rape and other anti-social behaviour.
3. **Family breakdown**, child neglect, quarrels and **poverty** in the home.
4. Lower **productivity** at work and absenteeism, so the economy suffers.
5. A high **cost of health care** for treating alcohol-related diseases, and a spread of **sexually transmitted infections** because of risky behaviour.
6. Early **school dropout** and loss of young people with good potential.

(Any five.)

questions.enonce_markdown: How may excessive alcohol consumption be combated? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Education and sensitisation** on the harmful effects of alcohol through the media, schools, churches and health talks.
2. **Laws**: forbid the sale of alcohol to **minors**, restrict the **hours and places** of sale, **ban advertising** and **raise taxes** and prices.
3. **Law enforcement**: fine or punish **drunk driving** (breath tests) and drunkenness in public.
4. **Counselling** and **treatment** of alcoholics in rehabilitation centres, with support groups such as Alcoholics Anonymous.
5. Providing young people with **recreational activities**, sports and **employment**, and **good parental and religious guidance**.
6. Putting **health warnings** on bottles.

(Any five.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Beside alcohol, name THREE other drugs common among youths and their harmful effects on youths. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Drug | Harmful effects on youths |
|---|---|
| **Tobacco (cigarettes, nicotine)** | **Addiction**; **lung cancer**, bronchitis and coughing; heart disease and high blood pressure; reduced physical fitness |
| **Indian hemp (cannabis, marijuana)** | **Hallucinations**, laziness and **loss of memory**; **mental disorders**; damage to the lungs; poor results at school; addiction |
| **Cocaine or heroin** | Strong **addiction**; **mental illness** and aggressive behaviour; loss of appetite and **malnutrition**; damage to the nose, heart and liver; risk of **death by overdose**; **HIV infection** from shared needles |

Other drugs that can be named: tramadol and other **stimulants** or pills (amphetamines), **kola nut and coffee** (caffeine) and **glue or petrol sniffing**.
